summary: This image presents a comparison of feedback questionnaire results between two groups: template-based and LLM-based approaches. The violin plots illustrate the distribution and mean scores of responses on a Likert scale from 1 to 7 for various questions. Key findings include that the question 'Did questions help in the selection of unviable goals?' has a p-value of 0.34, while 'Did questions help to improve a plan?' shows a p-value of 0.01, indicating significant improvement with LLM-based methods. Other questions include 'Did the possibility to ask questions reduce the level of difficulty?' (p-value 0.02), 'How confident are you that you know which plans are possible?' (p-value 0.67), 'How satisfied are you with your task?' (p-value 0.51), and 'How easy was the task for you?' (p-value 0.26). The LLM-based approach significantly outperforms the template-based method in helping participants improve their plans and reduce difficulty.
